flow.title: One engine. Three jobs.
flow.lede: A normal hotel buys power from STEG and burns gas for hot water. More than half of a power station's fuel leaves as waste heat. Trigeneration catches that heat on your site and uses it.

meta.title: How it works
meta.description: How one gas engine makes a hotel's electricity, hot water and cooling, which Tunisian hotels it fits, and how our screening tool decides.

hero.title: One engine.
hero.lede: A gas engine on site makes electricity. Its waste heat makes hot water. In summer, an absorption chiller turns spare heat into cold water for air conditioning.

diagram.title: Where the gas goes
diagram.label: Energy flow: {elec}% of the gas becomes electricity, {heat}% becomes useful heat for hot water, the pool and the absorption chiller, and {loss}% is lost.
diagram.caption: Total efficiency about {total}%, against roughly half for a power station and a separate boiler. Central values from the engine model.

why.title: Why Tunisian hotels.
why.lede: Hotels need power, hot water and cooling at the same time, all year. Tunisia makes its electricity from gas, and pays most for it at the summer peak.

fit.title: Who it fits.
yesItems: Large hotels, with a big and steady heat demand
Open all year, so the engine runs in winter too
A heated pool, spa or thalasso
A connection to the STEG gas network
noItems: Small or seasonal hotels: the engine would sit idle half the year
No heated pool and little hot water
Cooled by split units with no chilled-water loop

decides.title: How the tool decides.
decides.lede: Four answers about your hotel. The tool tries every engine size, keeps the one that pays back fastest, and runs it three times.

scenarios.title: Three scenarios
scenarios.body: Sceptical, central and enthusiastic values for every assumption. You see a range, not a single promise.

verdict.title: One verdict
verdict.body: Good fit up to {good} years of central payback. Possible fit up to {possible} years. Weak fit beyond that, or below {hours} full-load hours a year.

sources.title: Every assumption cited
sources.body: Gas and electricity tariffs, engine costs, efficiencies and occupancy, each with its source.

study.title: What a feasibility study adds.
study.lede: The screening uses typical hotels. A study uses yours. One installer quote moves the answer more than any other input.

visit.title: Site visit
visit.body: Plant room, gas meter, roof and space for a chiller.

bills.title: Your real bills
bills.body: Twelve months of STEG electricity and gas, hour by hour where the meter allows.

quote.title: Installer quotes
quote.body: Real prices replace our cost curve: the biggest unknown in the screening.

report.title: A bankable report
report.body: Sizing, cash flow and the FTE subsidy file, ready for your bank.

cost.q: What does a feasibility study cost?
cost.a: It depends on the hotel's size and the data available. We send a price after a first call. The screening is always free.

accuracy.q: How accurate is the free screening?
accuracy.a: It is a screening, not a study. It uses a typical hotel for your size and city, and shows a range from favourable to unfavourable. The study replaces those assumptions with your data.

fte.q: Does the FTE subsidy apply to hotels?
fte.a: We don't know yet. The Energy Transition Fund supports cogeneration in industry, and hotel eligibility is unconfirmed. That is why the subsidy never enters our headline payback.

blackout.q: Will the plant keep the hotel running during a grid cut?
blackout.a: Not as modelled. The screening assumes a grid-connected plant. Running in island mode needs extra equipment, which a study can price.

noGas.q: What if the hotel has no gas connection?
noGas.a: Then the plant needs one first, or another fuel. The study checks this on site.

install.a: No. We screen, study and refer you to installers. That keeps our advice independent of the equipment sold.
